headline: Amazon triples Nvidia chip order, adds 2M Blackwell, Rubin GPUs to AWS
summary: The multi-billion dollar deal includes next-gen Blackwell Ultra, Rubin, and Rubin Ultra GPUs, set to deploy across AWS data centers in 2027 and 2028.
details: Amazon and Nvidia have expanded their partnership, with Amazon ordering an additional 2 million Nvidia GPU chips for its data centers. These include the next-gen Blackwell Ultra, Rubin, and Rubin Ultra GPUs, slated for deployment across Amazon Web Services (AWS) in 2027 and 2028.

This massive order follows a previous agreement just five months ago for over 1 million Nvidia GPUs. Nvidia stated that demand has since "exceeded those expectations," making the new deal worth tens of billions of dollars.

The expanded collaboration goes beyond just chip purchases. Nvidia's networking hardware, open models, CPUs, data processing software, and robotics platform will also be integrated across AWS infrastructure.

This partnership grows even as Amazon invests heavily in its own competing AI chips, such as the Trainium for deep learning and the Arm-built Graviton CPU. Amazon's custom chip business recently crossed a $25 billion annualized revenue run rate.

Nvidia also plans to send an unspecified number of Vera CPUs, some integrated with Rubin, others standalone, to AWS. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang expects Vera to be deployed by every major hyperscaler, neocloud, AI lab, and system OEM.

Amazon will adopt Nvidia's full physical AI stack, including Omniverse, Cosmos, Isaac, and Jetson, to power its robot fleet. Additionally, AWS will host Nvidia's Nemotron family of open models on its Bedrock and SageMaker platforms.

Nvidia reported Q2 sales of $96.2 billion, with data center revenue at $89 billion, up 117% year-over-year. The company forecasts Q3 revenue of $108 billion and has committed $279 billion to secure supply and manufacturing capacity.

headline_marked: Galaxy S27 Ultra leak reveals [[7,000mAh battery Samsung reportedly rejected]] for next year's flagship
headline: Galaxy S27 Ultra leak reveals 7,000mAh battery Samsung reportedly rejected for next year's flagship
summary: Samsung reportedly tested a massive 7,000mAh battery for the Galaxy S27 Ultra, potentially ditching the S Pen, but sources suggest a smaller capacity for the final model.
details: Samsung reportedly experimented with a massive 7,000mAh battery for the upcoming Galaxy S27 Ultra, a significant jump from its usual 5,000mAh. This test model also apparently omitted the S Pen, suggesting a trade-off for increased power.

The information comes from X user Kro, picked up by Android Authority, indicating Samsung's internal testing. This move could have offered users significantly longer battery life, a feature many desire.

However, the final retail version of the Galaxy S27 Ultra is now rumored to feature a 5,700mAh or 6,000mAh battery. It is still expected to utilize silicon-carbon anode technology, similar to what's seen in the Fold 8 devices.

Samsung has maintained a 5,000mAh battery in its flagship Ultra phones since the S20 Ultra, while competitors offer larger capacities and faster charging. Overseas brands are pushing limits with batteries up to 7,300mAh and 240W charging speeds.

Beyond battery, the Galaxy S27 Ultra is also rumored to feature a revamped design, moving away from its familiar camera setup. While unconfirmed, this leak suggests a significant visual refresh for the device.
